title: A recurrent neural network uncovers a non-canonical human GRHL1 DNA-binding site
summary: A convolutional recurrent neural network found 46 GRHL1 ChIP-seq sites missed by a conventional position-weight matrix, including sequences lacking the previously considered obligatory CNNG motif. Isothermal titration calorimetry confirmed GRHL1 binding to a selected non-canonical sequence lacking that core motif; nucleotide mutagenesis experiments also showed that model scores tracked measured affinity across tested variants.
ai_technology: Convolutional recurrent neural network trained on GRHL1 HT-SELEX binding data
organization: Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin; Max Delbrück Center for Molecular Medicine; Hannover Medical School; Institute of Bioorganic Chemistry, Polish Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: Isothermal titration calorimetry confirmed GRHL1 binding to a selected non-canonical sequence lacking that core motif; nucleotide mutagenesis experiments also showed that model scores tracked measured affinity across tested variants.
evidence.unknown: Only one of the 46 predicted non-canonical sites was directly validated by ITC in this study; 46 is a model-nominated set, not 46 experimentally confirmed bindings. Biochemical affinity was tested with the isolated GRHL1 DNA-binding domain and synthetic DNA, not in vivo transcriptional effects for the novel site.
evidence.ai_role: The CNN/RNN learned GRHL1 sequence-binding patterns from HT-SELEX and scored human-cell ChIP-seq peaks. It identified 46 sites not detected by FIMO/PWM; one selected high-scoring non-canonical site was experimentally confirmed by ITC, and predicted variant affinity changes were compared with ITC results.
